_readme: The bench the hw tests run on, as data: which output drives which input, with the probe/vdiv/offset the capture must be configured for and the signal it must then see. Rewiring the bench means editing this file, never a test. A link that is not declared here is not guessed: the test that needs it skips and names what is declared. Scope today: the awg_to_a0 scenario (one generator into one analog channel); the other links are listed under undeclared until tests use them. Checked offline by tests/unit/test_bench_declaration.py; used by tests/hardware (markers: hw, hwsoak).

awg_to_a0.summary: M454 AWG (MCX output) straight into analog channel A0, direct coax, no probe, no divider
awg_to_a0._tolerance_note: level_v is the absolute slack on the declared levels: it covers the generator's own accuracy and an uncalibrated 8-bit ADC (measured 3.13 Vpp for a 3 V program), while a wrong probe or a divider is a factor of 10 out (2.7 V) and still fails

undeclared: calibration output (1 kHz, front panel pin) -> any channel

soak._readme: Budgets and thresholds of the long-run group. Durations are tiers; --soak-seconds overrides the tier for one run. Every number here is a check the run asserts, not a comment. rss_after_warmup_mib bounds the growth left after the allocator warm-up, measured as the median of the last quarter of the samples against the first quarter (a cold stream process climbs 57 -> 119 MiB in that first quarter, a warm one grows 0.4 MiB over the whole run); rss_steady_mib is the leak check: inside the last quarter it takes the median pairwise slope (a climb every pair agrees on) and the level at the end of the quarter against the higher of its start and the peak the run already reached (a step that stays, each end at least three samples so one sample is a spike), reports the larger, and a release is negative in both and floors at zero; growth below the earlier peak is the allocator's swing, not growth. It judges nothing below rss_steady_min_samples: the 60 s tier has 12-162 samples, and there the knee (26 MiB over the first ~15 cycles) and the ~1.5 MiB per-cycle staircase are both larger than the 8 MiB bound — the same bench measured 32-42 MiB of net growth at 60 s against 11 MiB over 10 min and 1 h, so a verdict from a 60 s window would be knee, not leak.

manual: unplug / replug the USB cable while a run is active, then `openm454 recover`
suspend and resume the host in the middle of a stream
exhaust the Linux usbfs budget (usbfs_memory_mb) and check the NO_MEM hint path
power-cycle the scope and verify the next open reloads the FPGA
reprogram the generator while a run is armed (the stop handshake owns the link: refused by design)
